skills.name: Initialize Monorepo Structure

testcases.name: root package.json declares frontend and backend workspaces

skills.capability: Create the root repository scaffold with frontend/ and backend/ workspace directories, a root package.json wiring npm workspaces, .gitignore, and a base README.
skills.prompt_template: You are setting up the root of a monorepo containing a React+Vite frontend and a Node/Express backend as npm workspaces. Create frontend/ and backend/ directories, a root package.json with a workspaces array listing both, and a .gitignore covering node_modules, dist, build, and .env. Do not add any domain/business logic — this is scaffolding only.
acceptance_criteria: Root package.json declares an npm workspaces array including 'frontend' and 'backend'
Running npm install from the repo root succeeds and installs dependencies for both workspaces without error

skills.name: Scaffold Vite React Frontend

testcases.name: frontend package.json declares react and vite dependencies

skills.capability: Generate the frontend/ workspace as a Vite + React 18 app with Tailwind CSS configured and building successfully.
skills.prompt_template: You are scaffolding the frontend/ workspace using Vite with the React 18 template, then adding and configuring Tailwind CSS (tailwind.config.js, postcss.config.js, base directives in the main CSS file). Keep the generated App component minimal — no domain UI, just a placeholder confirming the build pipeline works.
acceptance_criteria: frontend/package.json lists react and react-dom at ^18 and vite as dependencies
frontend/package.json lists tailwindcss, postcss, and autoprefixer as devDependencies
Running npm run dev in frontend/ starts the Vite dev server without error

skills.name: Scaffold Express Backend
skills.capability: Generate the backend/ workspace as a minimal Node.js + Express application with an entrypoint server file and a placeholder health route.
skills.prompt_template: You are scaffolding the backend/ workspace as a Node.js Express server. Create a package.json with express as a dependency, an entrypoint (e.g. src/index.js) that starts the server on a configurable port, and a GET /api/health route returning a 200 JSON status payload. No domain routes or data models — scaffolding only.
acceptance_criteria: backend/package.json lists express as a dependency
Starting the backend server (e.g. npm start or node src/index.js) listens on the configured port without throwing

skills.name: Configure Vitest Test Framework

testcases.name: frontend package.json declares a test script
backend package.json declares a test script

skills.capability: Wire up Vitest as the shared test runner across both frontend (jsdom + React Testing Library) and backend (node environment) workspaces with a working npm test script.
skills.prompt_template: You are configuring Vitest as the test framework for both workspaces. Add vitest as a devDependency to frontend/ and backend/, add a 'test' npm script to each package.json that runs vitest, and add a vitest.config.js in frontend/ that sets test.environment to 'jsdom' and wires @testing-library/react. Do not write feature tests here, only the framework configuration.
acceptance_criteria: frontend/package.json and backend/package.json each declare a 'test' script invoking vitest
Running npm test from the repo root executes both workspaces' suites and exits 0 on a fresh checkout

skills.name: Create .adlc.json Config
skills.capability: Generate a root .adlc.json declaring the test command, tech stack, and required services (none beyond local SQLite/JSON file store) for downstream agent tooling.
skills.prompt_template: You are authoring the root .adlc.json file consumed by the agent pipeline. Populate test_command with the exact command that runs the full test suite (e.g. 'npm test'), tech_stack with an array naming the key technologies (react, vite, tailwindcss, express, vitest), and required_services as an empty array since the app only needs a local SQLite or JSON file store with no external services.
acceptance_criteria: .adlc.json contains a non-empty test_command string that runs the test suite
.adlc.json tech_stack array includes react, express, and vitest
.adlc.json required_services is an empty array (no external services required)

skills.name: Configure ESLint and Prettier Baseline

testcases.name: frontend package.json declares a lint script
backend package.json declares a lint script

skills.capability: Set up a shared ESLint + Prettier baseline covering both the React frontend and Node backend, with lint/format npm scripts wired in each workspace.
skills.prompt_template: You are configuring linting and formatting baselines for both workspaces. Add eslint and prettier as devDependencies, create an ESLint config appropriate to each workspace (React/JSX rules for frontend, Node rules for backend), a shared .prettierrc, and 'lint' and 'format' npm scripts in each package.json. Keep rule sets minimal defaults — no custom domain rules.
acceptance_criteria: frontend/package.json and backend/package.json each declare a 'lint' script invoking eslint
An ESLint config file exists for each workspace defining rules appropriate to its environment (React for frontend, Node for backend)
Running npm run lint in each workspace completes with zero errors against the scaffolded baseline code

skills.name: Add CI Smoke Test Suite
skills.capability: Write a minimal end-to-end smoke test pair — a backend API health-check test and a frontend basic component render test — proving the scaffolded environment builds and tests execute successfully.
skills.prompt_template: You are adding the minimal smoke tests that prove the newly scaffolded environment works end-to-end. In backend/, write a test that hits GET /api/health and asserts a 200 response with a status field. In frontend/, write a test that renders the placeholder App component and asserts it mounts without throwing. These are the only tests to add — no domain feature coverage.
acceptance_criteria: A backend test asserts GET /api/health responds 200 with a JSON status field
A frontend test renders the base App component without throwing
Running npm test from the repo root executes both smoke tests and the overall command exits 0
